definitions.explanation: A message sent between computers or mobile devices over a network; the full Japanese term for email. Commonly shortened to just メール in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {電子|でんし}メールを{送|おく}る。
{電子|でんし}メールで{書類|しょるい}を{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
examples.english: Please submit the documents by email.

examples.japanese: お{問|と}い{合|あ}わせは、{電子|でんし}メールまたは{電話|でんわ}でお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: For inquiries, please contact us by email or telephone.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{電子|でんし}メールよりもチャットアプリで{連絡|れんらく}を{取|と}る{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, more people use chat apps rather than email to stay in touch.

notes:
Composed of {電子|でんし} (electronic) + メール (mail, from English). The formal, full-length term for email, used in official notices, legal documents, business forms, and signage — places where the casual shortened form メール would feel too informal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電子|でんし}メールを{送|おく}る: to send an email
- {電子|でんし}メールを{受|う}け{取|と}る: to receive an email
- {電子|でんし}メールアドレス: email address
- {電子|でんし}メールで{連絡|れんらく}する: to contact by email
- {電子|でんし}メールマガジン: email newsletter

SIMILAR WORDS:
- メール: mail / email — the everyday shortened form; far more common in conversation. Ambiguously refers to email, SMS, or messaging depending on context.
- Eメール: e-mail — another written form, seen on forms and older materials.
- メッセージ: message — broader; includes chat app messages, SMS, etc.

USAGE:
In conversation, simply say メール. Use {電子|でんし}メール in formal writing, government documents, or when explicitly distinguishing email from other kinds of messages (such as postal mail, SMS, or in-app chat). Historically the formal term was needed to distinguish email from {郵便|ゆうびん} (postal mail), but as email became ubiquitous the short form took over.
